title: Focus trail and heading outline
blurb: A canvas draws a form and, when focus moves, a ring that flies from the old control to the new one while the rest is shaded. It can also mark the size of each touch target and join each label to its control. A second canvas draws an article with its headings listed beside it. Each row of the list is the heading's own pixels.
question: Can a canvas show where focus went, how large each target is, which label names which control and what the heading outline is, using only the elements it draws and the positions the browser reports for them?
result: Yes in Chromium 157. focusin and getBoundingClientRect() are enough for the trail, and a rectangle of the article's picture is enough for an outline row. The browser's own focus ring is in the picture only when the focused element is inside the drawable element, and it is cut at that element's border box.
